title: Warmup policy: weight prefetch + KV-seeding strategy to minimize cold starts on Dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and implement a warmup policy for Dedicated capacity that combines model weight prefetching, KV cache seeding, and coordinated fleet controls to reduce cold-start latency and preserve throughput guarantees under autoscaling events.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start median latency for 8k context models reduced by >= 50% compared to baseline cold replicas
KV cache hit-rate on newly added nodes > 60% within first 30s for typical chat workloads
Autoscaler can scale up/down without violating throughput SLAs when warmup policy is enabled
Feature toggle exists (console + API flag) to enable/disable warmup per allocation and per model
background: Customers using Dedicated pools report tail latency spikes and throughput drops when autoscaler adds new replicas during traffic spikes. Current warm-pool behavior loads weights lazily and does not seed KV caches, leading to a multi-second first-response penalty and throughput instability. This ticket scopes a coordinated solution across runtime, autoscaler, and fleet control plane.
design_decisions: Use two-stage warmup: (1) weight prefetch to memory (cold->warmed) with low-priority I/O, (2) KV-seeding via sampled request replay to pre-populate frequent prefix entries.
Maintain a lightweight warm state (no active worker threads) for preloaded weights to reduce resource cost while allowing fast activation.
Limit number of prewarmed replicas per shard based on memory headroom and estimated warmup IOPS to avoid affecting steady-state throughput.
Prefer asynchronous KV seeding in background; fall back to on-demand seeding on highly memory-constrained customers.
Expose warmup budget and seeding aggressiveness in Dedicated policy config (default conservative for multi-tenant/mixed-VM fleets).
tradeoffs: Aggressive prefetch/seeding reduces cold-starts but increases transient I/O and memory pressure which could impact running replicas. We chose conservative defaults and adaptive throttling (backoff when IO stalls detected). Full eager seeding increases cost; customers can opt-in for stricter throughput guarantees.
implementation_plan: Runtime: Add weight-prefetch API to loader with low-priority I/O and validate Mmap/prefetch paths for Linux kernels (ENG-12846)
Runtime: Implement KV-seed worker that replays high-frequency prefixes from a sampled request log (ENG-12847)
Autoscaler: Add 'prewarm_count' config and prewarm lifecycle hook to trigger weight prefetch prior to adding active replica (ENG-12848)
Control plane: UI and API flags for warmup budget, seeding aggressiveness, and per-model opt-in (PM-4421)
E2E: Integration test harness to simulate scale-up under load and measure latency/throughput (ENG-12849)
Observability: Add warmup metrics (prefetch_progress, kv_seed_rate, prewarmed_replicas, warm_activation_latency) and dashboard tiles (console-2026.03)
Rollout: feature-flagged rollout to internal Dedicated clusters -> early beta customers -> general availability
